title: Cap. II: Semipelagians — initiative from us; perseverance by free will
pass_a_gloss: The Semipelagians have embraced Pelagius's poisoned dogma in part; in which number are Faustus of Riez, Cassian the Conferencer, the Massilians, and all others who, confessing the necessity of grace for living piously, persevering in piety, and obtaining eternal life, nevertheless defend that from us there precedes a certain beginning of labor and striving, which Divine grace follows, and in view of which this saving grace is given to us. They also hold consequently that after a human by striving and laboring has obtained God's grace, he perseveres in this grace, faith, and good works not through some gift that flows from election, but through his free choice; and that from the foresight of such a will he is elected unto eternal life. Key lemmas: Semipelagiani; initium laboris & conatus (beginning of labor and striving); Faustus Regiensis; Cassianus; Massilienses; praescientia voluntatis.
pass_b_english: The Semipelagians took up part of Pelagius's poison. Count among them Faustus of Riez, Cassian the Conferencer, the Massilians, and all who admit grace is needed to live godly, persevere, and reach eternal life — yet still claim that from us there first comes a beginning of labor and effort, which God's grace then follows, and for the sake of which saving grace is given. Consequently they hold that once a person has gained God's grace by striving and labor, he stays in that grace, faith, and good works not by any gift flowing from election, but by his own free choice; and that election to eternal life rests on foresight of that will.
source_text: Pelagii venenatum dogma Semipelagiani ex parte amplexi sunt; in queis numero Faustum Regiensem, Cassianum Collatorem, Massilienses, aliosque omnes, qui confitentes gratiae necessitatem ad pie vivendum, in pietate perseverandum, & vitam aeternam consequendam, defendunt tamen ex nobis praecedere quoddam initium laboris & conatus, quod Divina gratia subsequitur, & cujus intuitu haec gratia salutaris nobis donatur. Tenent etiam consequenter, postquam homo conando & laborando Dei gratiam adeptus est, non per donum aliquod quod manat ab electione, sed per liberum arbitrium suum perseverare in hac gratia, fide, & bonis operibus; atque ex praescientia talis voluntatis eligi ad vitam aeternam.
